SOLMERE ENERGY — SUBSTATION OUTAGE INCIDENT REPORT
Facility: Substation 12, Millbrook District | Report No. GRID-INC-0204
Incident Date: July 8 | Report Date: July 14
Prepared by: Grid Operations (Lead: Piotr Zielinski)

INCIDENT SUMMARY
At 3:22 p.m. on July 8, a voltage regulator at Substation 12 failed, causing an unplanned outage affecting approximately 2,800 customers in the surrounding district. Power was restored to all affected customers by 4:02 p.m., a total outage duration of 40 minutes, after field crews manually switched the affected feeder to an adjacent substation's capacity while the failed regulator was isolated.

ROOT CAUSE
The failed regulator's control board suffered a component failure consistent with age-related degradation. The unit was installed 22 years ago, 2 years beyond the manufacturer's recommended 20-year service life for this regulator model. Inspection found no evidence of external damage, storm activity, or overload; the failure is attributed to normal end-of-life degradation of the control board's capacitors.

UNRELATED EVENT: SUBSTATION 8 MAINTENANCE
Separately, Substation 8, in a different district, had a previously scheduled and customer-communicated maintenance outage on the same day, July 8, from 1:00 p.m. to 1:30 p.m., unrelated to Substation 12's equipment failure. Some customer inquiries conflated the two events given the same-day timing; this report clarifies they are unrelated: Substation 8's outage was planned maintenance with no equipment failure, while Substation 12's was an unplanned failure of an aged component.

FLEET CONTEXT
Grid Operations maintains 34 substations district-wide. Of these, 6 substations, including Substation 12, have voltage regulators installed more than 20 years ago, beyond the manufacturer's recommended service life. An additional 11 substations have regulators between 15 and 20 years old, within recommended service life but approaching it. The remaining 17 substations have regulators installed within the last 15 years and are not considered near-term replacement candidates.

DISCUSSION OF RESPONSE OPTIONS
Following this incident, one proposal was to replace all regulators over 15 years old immediately across all 17 affected substations, 6 over 20 years plus 11 between 15 and 20 years, at an estimated cost of $4.2 million. This was discussed and not adopted as an immediate blanket replacement; leadership determined the 11 regulators still within their recommended service life do not present the same near-term risk as the 6 already past it. Instead, the company is funding immediate replacement of all 6 regulators over 20 years old, including Substation 12's now-failed unit, at an estimated cost of $1.1 million this year, with the remaining 11 regulators between 15 and 20 years old to be evaluated for replacement in next year's capital planning cycle based on updated risk assessment.

CUSTOMER COMMUNICATIONS
Customer notifications were sent within 15 minutes of the outage start, consistent with the 20-minute target in the emergency communications policy. Estimated restoration time was updated once at 3:50 p.m. when field crews confirmed the feeder-switch approach would restore power faster than waiting for a full regulator repair on site.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Replace all 6 regulators over 20 years old, including Substation 12's, by year end, at an estimated $1.1 million.
2. Evaluate the remaining 11 regulators between 15 and 20 years old for next year's capital planning cycle.
3. No blanket replacement of all 17 aging regulators this year, per the discussion above.

CUSTOMER CREDIT POLICY
Per state regulatory requirements, customers experiencing an unplanned outage over 30 minutes are automatically credited $15 on their next bill. All 2,800 affected customers on Substation 12's feeder will receive this credit automatically; no customer action is required to claim it, and the credits will be applied within the next two billing cycles following this report's approval.

SIGN-OFF
Approved by Piotr Zielinski, Grid Operations Lead, July 14.

MERIDIAN CLOUD SYSTEMS — SECURITY INCIDENT REPORT
Incident Reference: SEC-0447 | Classification: Confirmed data exposure, PII (no credentials or payment data)
Prepared by: Security Team (Lead: Yuki Tanaka) | Report Date: October 3

DISCOVERY
On October 1, an external security researcher, operating under Meridian's public bug-bounty program, reported that a cloud storage bucket used for customer-onboarding document uploads was configured with public read access, allowing anyone with the bucket's URL to list and download its full contents without authentication of any kind whatsoever.

SCOPE OF EXPOSURE
Investigation confirmed the bucket had been misconfigured with public read access since September 23, 8 days before discovery, following a deployment that inadvertently reset the bucket's access policy during an infrastructure migration. The bucket contained onboarding documents for 3,400 customer accounts, including customer names and email addresses used during account setup. The bucket did NOT contain passwords, payment card data, or authentication credentials of any kind, which are stored in a separate, unaffected system with different access controls entirely.

VERIFICATION OF OTHER STORAGE
As part of the investigation, the security team also reviewed a separate analytics-logs bucket used for internal usage metrics, since it uses a similar naming convention to the affected bucket and was checked out of caution. That bucket was found to be correctly configured with private access throughout, was not affected by the September 23 migration, and shows no evidence of any unauthorized access; it is mentioned here only to document that it was checked and cleared, not because it was part of the actual exposure.

ACCESS LOG ANALYSIS
Cloud provider access logs for the affected bucket show requests from the reporting researcher's IP address, consistent with responsible discovery, and a small number of automated scanner requests from unrelated third-party security-scanning services that routinely probe for public buckets across the internet; none of the automated scanner traffic appears to have downloaded bucket contents, only listed the bucket's existence.

REMEDIATION
The bucket's access policy was corrected within 40 minutes of the report being received on October 1, restoring private access. All 3,400 affected customers were notified by email on October 4, and the company's standard identity-monitoring offer was extended to affected customers as a precaution, even though no credential or payment data was involved in this exposure.

BUG BOUNTY DISCUSSION
The reporting researcher initially requested a $50,000 payment, citing the number of records involved. Meridian's bug-bounty program has published, tiered payouts based on vulnerability category rather than records-affected count; this finding falls under the program's "misconfigured access control, PII exposure" category, which is published at $2,500. Security team leadership discussed making an exception and paying the researcher's requested $50,000 given the record count, but ultimately did not adopt that exception, since doing so on an ad hoc basis would undermine the published, consistent tier structure for all future researchers. After the program terms were explained, the researcher accepted the standard $2,500 payout under the published category.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Add automated post-deployment verification that flags any storage bucket with public read access within 15 minutes of a deployment, rather than relying on discovery by outside researchers.
2. Review all infrastructure-migration scripts for similar access-policy reset risk by November 1.
3. No change recommended to the published bug-bounty tier structure, per the discussion above.

FOLLOW-UP MONITORING
Security will run a full audit of all customer-facing storage buckets across the company within 30 days, cross-checked against the new automated verification tool once deployed, to confirm no other buckets carry a similar public-access misconfiguration from this or any prior infrastructure migration performed in the last two years.

SIGN-OFF
Approved by Yuki Tanaka, Security Team Lead, October 3.

ALDERPOINT HEALTH — BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING MINUTES
Date: October 21 | Recorded by: Miriam Castellano, Board Secretary

ATTENDANCE
Present: Chair Gideon Farley, Directors Consuela Marques, Tariq Idris, Wanjiru Kamau, and Priyanka Chatterjee. CEO Beatrice Adeyemi and CFO Samir Kassab were also present throughout.

QUALITY METRICS REVIEW
CEO Adeyemi presented Q3 quality metrics: patient satisfaction score of 87%, up from 84% in Q2, and 30-day readmission rate of 8.2%, under the board's 10% target ceiling, an improvement from 9.1% last quarter. Both metrics were presented for informational review; no board action was required or taken on this item, as the metrics are tracked administratively rather than requiring board approval each quarter.

CAPITAL PROJECT: OUTPATIENT SURGERY WING
CFO Kassab presented a capital proposal to construct a new outpatient surgery wing, adding 6 operating rooms and pre/post-operative recovery space, at a total project cost of $28 million, to be funded through a combination of $18 million in existing capital reserves and a $10 million bond issuance. The proposal responds to consistently high utilization of existing outpatient surgery capacity, currently operating above 95% scheduled capacity on weekdays. After discussion of the bond terms and construction timeline, estimated at 18 months, Tariq Idris moved to approve the $28 million outpatient surgery wing project. Wanjiru Kamau seconded. The motion passed 5-0.

CAPITAL PROJECT: PROPOSED INPATIENT TOWER (DEFERRED)
Separately, CFO Kassab presented a larger, more preliminary proposal for a new inpatient tower, adding 80 beds, at an estimated cost of $45 million, to address projected bed-capacity constraints over the next decade based on regional population growth projections. Given the size of this proposal relative to the outpatient wing already on the table, and the more preliminary state of its feasibility study, Consuela Marques moved to defer the inpatient tower proposal, directing management to complete a full feasibility study, including updated demand projections and financing options, for presentation at the board's next quarterly meeting. The motion to defer passed 5-0. No funds were committed to the inpatient tower proposal at this meeting.

FINANCING DISCUSSION
Samir Kassab clarified that the $10 million bond issuance for the outpatient wing is a separate financing action from any potential future financing for the inpatient tower, and that approving the outpatient wing tonight does not commit the organization's bonding capacity in a way that would preclude pursuing the larger tower project later if the board approves it after the feasibility study is complete.

STAFFING IMPLICATIONS
Beatrice Adeyemi noted the new outpatient wing is projected to require approximately 45 additional clinical and support staff once operational, a hiring plan to be developed over the 18-month construction period rather than all at once near opening.

OTHER BUSINESS
The board briefly discussed the upcoming annual community health needs assessment, due to the state by year end; Adeyemi confirmed it is on track for completion by the November board meeting, with a draft circulated to directors beforehand for comment.

MEDICAL STAFF UPDATE
Beatrice Adeyemi briefly updated the board on medical staff recruitment, noting two new cardiology hires starting next month, which she credited partly to the improved patient satisfaction scores discussed earlier making recruitment conversations noticeably easier than in prior years of active hiring.

GOVERNANCE ITEM
Priyanka Chatterjee reminded the board that annual conflict-of-interest disclosure forms are due back to the Board Secretary by November 1, ahead of the November meeting, consistent with the organization's bylaws requiring annual refiling regardless of whether anything has changed since the prior year's disclosure, and regardless of a director's tenure on the board.

ADJOURNMENT
Meeting adjourned at 5:15 p.m. Next meeting: November 18.

Minutes respectfully submitted by Miriam Castellano, Board Secretary.

Seller shall sell and Buyer shall purchase 6 new Model FL-800 electric forklifts, at a unit price of $38,000 each, for a total purchase price of $228,000, plus applicable delivery charges described in Section 3 below.

2. WARRANTY
Each forklift carries Seller's standard warranty covering parts and labor for 3 years or 6,000 operating hours, whichever occurs first, from the date of delivery. Seller offered Buyer an optional extended warranty upgrade, extending coverage to 5 years or 10,000 hours, at an additional cost of $3,200 per unit. 4. PAYMENT
Buyer shall pay 30% of the total purchase price, $68,400 for the forklifts plus the full $12,000 for the parts package, as a deposit upon signing, with the remaining balance due within 30 days of delivery.

5. TRAINING
Seller shall provide one on-site operator training session for up to 12 of Buyer's operators within 2 weeks of delivery, at no additional charge, covering safe operation and routine maintenance of the FL-800 model specifically.

6. WARRANTY EXCLUSIONS

DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM
Between Vantage Analytics LLC ("Controller") and CloudMailer, Inc. ("Processor")
Effective Date: October 1

1. SCOPE
This Data Processing Addendum ("DPA") governs Processor's processing of personal data on Controller's behalf solely for the purpose of transactional email delivery, account notifications, password resets, and billing receipts, on Controller's instructions, as described in the underlying Master Services Agreement between the parties.

2. PROCESSING INSTRUCTIONS
Processor shall process personal data only as instructed by Controller, only for the purpose described in Section 1, and shall not use personal data for Processor's own purposes, including marketing to the underlying data subjects.

3. DATA RETENTION
An earlier draft of this DPA, circulated September 10, proposed a 90-day retention period for delivery logs after each email is sent. Controller requested a shorter period during negotiation, and the parties agreed to the following, which governs: Processor shall retain email delivery logs, including recipient address and delivery status, for no more than 30 days after sending, solely for delivery troubleshooting purposes, after which such logs are automatically and permanently deleted from Processor's systems.

4. SUB-SUBPROCESSORS
Processor may engage sub-subprocessors to assist in providing the service, provided Processor gives Controller at least 30 days' advance written notice before engaging any new sub-subprocessor, during which Controller may object on reasonable data-protection grounds. If Controller objects and the parties cannot resolve the objection within 15 days, Controller may terminate the underlying Master Services Agreement without penalty as it relates to the affected processing.

5. SECURITY MEASURES
Processor shall maintain technical and organizational security measures appropriate to the risk, including encryption of personal data in transit and at rest, and shall maintain the SOC2 Type II certification referenced in the underlying Master Services Agreement for the duration of this DPA.

6. UNRELATED REFERENCE: SNAPINVOICE
For clarity, Controller separately uses a different subprocessor, SnapInvoice, for invoice-generation functions involving aggregate billing totals; that relationship is governed by its own, separate data processing terms and is not affected by, or part of, this DPA, which applies specifically and exclusively to Processor's email-delivery processing described in Section 1.

7. AUDIT RIGHTS
Controller may audit Processor's compliance with this DPA no more than once per 12-month period, upon 30 days' written notice, or without advance notice following a confirmed security incident affecting Controller's data.

8. TERMINATION AND DELETION
Upon termination of the underlying Master Services Agreement, Processor shall delete all personal data processed under this DPA within 30 days, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law, and shall certify such deletion in writing to Controller upon request.

9. GENERAL
This DPA supersedes the September 10 draft in its entirety and is incorporated into the underlying Master Services Agreement between the parties.

10. INTERNATIONAL TRANSFERS
To the extent Processor transfers personal data outside the region where Controller's customers are located, Processor shall implement appropriate safeguards consistent with applicable data-protection law, and shall notify Controller in advance of any new cross-border transfer arrangement not already disclosed as of the Effective Date above.

11. INCIDENT NOTIFICATION
Processor shall notify Controller without undue delay, and in any event within 48 hours, upon becoming aware of any security incident affecting personal data processed under this DPA, providing all information reasonably available at the time of notification and updating Controller as the investigation progresses.

12. LIABILITY
Each party's liability under this DPA is subject to the liability provisions of the underlying Master Services Agreement, and nothing in this DPA is intended to create liability broader than what that Agreement already establishes between the parties.

SIGNATURES
For Vantage Analytics LLC: Elliot Ferris, Director of Client Contracts
For CloudMailer, Inc.: Samir Kassab, VP Data Protection

BRIGHTPATH LEARNING — WEB ACCESSIBILITY COMPLIANCE AUDIT
Standard: WCAG 2.1 Level AA | Conducted by: Clarity Accessibility Partners, LLC
Audit Date: May 6-9 | Report Date: May 16

SCOPE
This audit evaluated BrightPath Learning's public website and course platform against WCAG 2.1 Level AA success criteria, covering the marketing homepage, course catalog pages, account and checkout flow, and the video-lecture player used across all courses on the platform today.

FINDINGS: HOMEPAGE AND COURSE CATALOG
The marketing homepage and course catalog pages were found substantially compliant with WCAG 2.1 Level AA, with no Level A or Level AA violations identified. Keyboard navigation, heading structure, and alt text for images all met the applicable success criteria on these pages.

FINDINGS: VIDEO-LECTURE PLAYER — CAPTIONS
The audit found that 340 of 566 total course videos, approximately 60%, lack closed captions entirely. Closed captions for pre-recorded video content are a WCAG 2.1 Level A success criterion, not Level AA, meaning this finding represents a more fundamental accessibility barrier than an AA-level issue, since Level A criteria are the baseline requirements that Level AA builds upon. This is classified as the audit's most significant finding overall.

FINDINGS: PROMOTIONAL BANNER COLOR CONTRAST
A secondary finding: the homepage's rotating promotional banner uses white text on a light-orange background with a contrast ratio of 3.2:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum required for normal-size text under WCAG 2.1 Level AA. This is a Level AA finding, less severe than the Level A captioning gap, and BrightPath's design team had already identified and scheduled a fix for this specific banner as part of an unrelated visual refresh planned for next month, independent of this audit's findings.

FINDINGS: CHECKOUT FLOW
The account creation and checkout flow was found fully compliant, with properly labeled form fields and appropriate error messaging that meets WCAG 2.1 Level AA requirements for form accessibility overall.

DISCUSSION OF RESPONSE OPTIONS
Given the scale of the captioning gap, one option discussed internally was pausing all new video uploads to the platform until 100% of the existing 566-video backlog is captioned. This was discussed and not adopted; leadership determined this would halt content production for an extended period without addressing the existing backlog any faster, and could harm the business without a corresponding accessibility benefit for existing users still facing the same barrier during the pause. Instead, BrightPath adopted a two-part response: all newly uploaded videos must include captions before publishing, effective immediately, and the 340-video backlog will be captioned on a rolling basis over 6 months, prioritized by course enrollment volume so the most-watched courses are captioned first.

REMEDIATION TIMELINE
1. Immediate: captions required for all new video uploads going forward, effective May 20.
2. 6-month rolling plan: caption the 340-video backlog, highest-enrollment courses first, complete by November 16.
3. Promotional banner contrast fix: already scheduled for next month's visual refresh, independent of this audit's findings.

FOLLOW-UP AUDIT
Clarity Accessibility Partners will conduct a follow-up audit of the video-lecture player specifically in November, to verify backlog captioning progress against the 6-month plan described above, and to re-confirm the homepage, catalog, and checkout flow remain compliant following any interim design changes made in the meantime.

INTERIM PROGRESS REPORTING
BrightPath's product team will provide monthly progress updates to the accessibility working group on captioning completion counts against the 340-video backlog, so that any slippage in the 6-month timeline is caught early rather than only being discovered at the November follow-up audit itself.

SIGN-OFF
Reviewed and accepted by BrightPath Learning's Head of Product, May 16, with a copy forwarded to the Legal team for awareness given the scale of the captioning finding.

CEDARVALE RETAIL GROUP — INVENTORY SHRINKAGE AUDIT
Subject: Annual Physical Inventory Count Reconciliation, Fiscal Year End
Prepared by: Internal Audit Office (Lead: Fatima Rashid)
Date Issued: February 3

METHODOLOGY
Physical inventory counts were conducted at all 40 store locations during the last week of the fiscal year and reconciled against perpetual inventory records maintained throughout the year. Shrinkage is calculated as the dollar value of the discrepancy, book inventory minus physical count, as a percentage of annual sales for that location. Company policy sets an acceptable shrinkage threshold of 2.0% of sales; locations exceeding this threshold are flagged for a follow-up loss-prevention investigation.

COMPANY-WIDE RESULTS
Company-wide average shrinkage this year was 1.6% of sales, consistent with the prior two years' average of 1.5%-1.7%, and comfortably within the acceptable range overall across the entire chain.

STORE #31 (FAIRVIEW) RESULTS
Store #31 recorded shrinkage of 1.8% of sales this year, within the 2.0% acceptable threshold, though slightly above the company-wide average of 1.6%. Given it remains under threshold, no follow-up investigation is triggered for Store #31 under current policy, though it will continue to be monitored given the slightly elevated rate relative to peers.

STORE #45 (RIDGEMONT) RESULTS
Store #45, a newer location opened 14 months ago, recorded shrinkage of 3.4% of sales this year, well above the 2.0% threshold. This is the only store exceeding threshold in this year's audit. Per policy, Store #45 is automatically flagged for a loss-prevention investigation, to begin within 30 days of this report.

PRELIMINARY OBSERVATIONS: STORE #45
While the full investigation is pending, Internal Audit's preliminary review noted Store #45 has had higher-than-average employee turnover in its first year, and its stockroom camera coverage was installed later than typical for a new store opening due to an equipment backorder, potentially providing more opportunity for either external theft or unrecorded internal loss during that gap; the investigation will determine the actual cause rather than this audit assuming one in advance.

DISCUSSION OF RESPONSE OPTIONS
Given Store #45's result, Loss Prevention proposed installing additional camera coverage at all 40 stores company-wide as a blanket preventive measure, estimated at $800,000. This was discussed and not adopted as an immediate company-wide rollout; leadership determined that only Store #45 shows an actual shrinkage problem this year, and a targeted investigation and response there is more appropriate than an $800,000 blanket rollout justified by a single outlier store. Additional camera coverage at Store #45 specifically, to close its existing coverage gap, was approved as part of the targeted response instead.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Complete Store #45's loss-prevention investigation within 30 days.
2. Install additional camera coverage at Store #45 specifically to close its existing gap.
3. Continue monitoring Store #31 given its shrinkage is above company average, though still under threshold.
4. No company-wide camera rollout this year, per the discussion above; revisit the question if additional stores exceed threshold in next year's audit cycle.

METHODOLOGY NOTE
This year's count reconciliation used the same barcode-scanning methodology as the prior two years, allowing direct year-over-year comparison of shrinkage rates without adjusting for any change in counting technique, which strengthens confidence that Store #45's elevated rate reflects an actual change in loss rather than a measurement artifact introduced by a new counting process or system.

DISTRIBUTION
This report has been shared with the Regional Vice President overseeing both Store #31 and Store #45, along with the Loss Prevention team assigned to lead the Store #45 investigation described above, and will be referenced again in next year's audit for trend comparison.

SIGN-OFF
Reviewed and accepted by Fatima Rashid, Lead Auditor, Internal Audit Office, February 3.

COBALT PEAK SOFTWARE — TRAVEL AND EXPENSE POLICY COMPLIANCE AUDIT
Subject: Q2 Executive Travel Expense Review
Prepared by: Internal Audit (Lead: Renata Silva)
Date Issued: July 20

SCOPE
This review examined all executive-level (VP and above) travel expense reports for Q2, focusing on compliance with Travel Policy TR-8, which requires economy or premium economy class for all flights under 6 hours, with business or first class permitted only for flights over 6 hours or with a pre-approved medical or accessibility exception on file with HR before travel occurs.

FINDING: BRAM VANDERMEER, JUNE 12 FLIGHT
Bram Vandermeer, VP People, expensed a first-class upgrade of $1,200 on a 3-hour domestic flight on June 12. No pre-approved medical or accessibility exception is on file for this trip, and the flight duration, 3 hours, is well under the 6-hour threshold that would otherwise permit first or business class. This is a policy violation under TR-8.

FINDING: CONSUELA MARQUES, JUNE 18 FLIGHT (FOR COMPARISON)
Separately, Consuela Marques, VP Engineering, expensed a similar business-class upgrade of $900 on a 4-hour domestic flight on June 18. However, a pre-approved medical accommodation is on file with HR, dated May 30, predating this trip, documenting a medical need for additional legroom. Per TR-8's exception provision, this upgrade is compliant, not a violation, despite the flight also being under 6 hours, because the pre-approved exception was properly on file before travel occurred.

ROOT CAUSE: VANDERMEER VIOLATION
When asked, Bram Vandermeer stated he was unaware his upgrade required either a longer flight or a pre-approved exception, and believed his executive level alone permitted flexibility on cabin class. Travel Policy TR-8 does not grant blanket cabin-class flexibility based on seniority alone; the 6-hour and exception rules apply uniformly regardless of an employee's level or title.

REMEDIATION
Per policy, Bram Vandermeer has been asked to reimburse the company the $1,200 difference between his economy fare and the first-class upgrade, due within 30 days. HR will also circulate a reminder of TR-8's terms to all VP-level staff, clarifying that seniority does not itself justify a cabin-class exception of any kind.

DISCUSSION OF POLICY RESPONSE
Given this finding, one Audit Committee member proposed eliminating flight upgrades entirely, even for documented medical or accessibility exceptions, to simplify enforcement and remove any ambiguity going forward. This was discussed and not adopted; Legal advised that removing the medical/accessibility exception pathway entirely could raise reasonable-accommodation concerns for employees with a genuine documented need, like Consuela Marques's case above, and that the actual problem in this audit was a policy-awareness gap for one executive, not a flaw in the exception process itself.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Bram Vandermeer to reimburse $1,200 within 30 days.
2. HR to circulate a TR-8 policy reminder to all VP-level staff, clarifying no seniority-based exception exists.
3. No change to the medical/accessibility exception provision in TR-8, per the discussion above.

SCOPE LIMITATION
This review covered only VP-level and above expense reports for Q2; a separate, ongoing quarterly sample audit covers director-level and below travel expenses under a different, lower-dollar sampling threshold, and is reported separately from this executive-focused review to the Audit Committee each quarter as its own item.

FOLLOW-UP
Internal Audit will confirm Bram Vandermeer's $1,200 reimbursement is received by the August 19 deadline and will note any non-payment in next quarter's follow-up summary to the Audit Committee, consistent with standard tracking for all open remediation items across the organization.

DISTRIBUTION
This report has been shared with the Audit Committee and with Bram Vandermeer's and Consuela Marques's direct manager, the CEO, for awareness, consistent with standard practice for any finding involving VP-level travel expenses at this level of seniority within the organization.

SIGN-OFF
Reviewed and accepted by Renata Silva, Lead Auditor, Internal Audit, July 20.

#it-postmortem channel — exported meeting chat notes, April 2 retro for the March 29 ERP outage

[10:00] Anouk V.: Starting retro for the March 29 ERP outage. Quick recap: ERP was down 3 hours, 1:00am-4:00am, during our scheduled monthly patch window.
[10:02] Marcus O.: to be clear up front, the patch itself applied successfully and is not the cause, right? want to make sure that's not where people's minds go first
[10:03] Anouk V.: correct, confirmed the patch installed cleanly, that's not the issue
[10:05] Anouk V.: what happened: as part of the patch window, we do a planned database failover to the standby replica as a safety step before patching primary. that failover failed to complete, leaving both primary and standby in an inconsistent state that the ERP application couldn't connect to properly, hence the 3-hour outage while we manually recovered
[10:10] Piotr Z.: why did the failover fail?
[10:15] Anouk V.: found it, the standby replica's replication lag was at 45 seconds at the moment of failover, but our failover automation is configured to abort if lag exceeds 30 seconds, to avoid failing over to a replica that's too far behind. the automation correctly aborted per its config, but the abort left things in a half-transitioned state that needed manual cleanup rather than cleanly rolling back
[10:20] Marcus O.: so two issues: the lag was too high to safely fail over in the first place, and separately, the abort path itself isn't clean
[10:21] Anouk V.: exactly, both need fixing
[10:25] Piotr Z.: why was replication lag at 45 seconds, is that normal?
[10:30] Anouk V.: checked, that's higher than typical, normal lag is usually under 10 seconds. traced it to an unusually large batch job that happened to be running against primary right at patch-window time, which our scheduling doesn't currently prevent from overlapping with the patch window
[10:35] Marcus O.: unrelated side note, our email system also had its own scheduled maintenance window that same night, totally separate system, no connection to the ERP issue, just happened to be the same night on the calendar
[10:36] Anouk V.: right, good to note but not related, different system entirely, different team even
[10:40] Piotr Z.: what's the fix plan?
[10:42] Anouk V.: three things: block batch jobs from running during the patch window's replication check, fix the abort path so it cleanly rolls back instead of leaving a half-transitioned state, and add automated failover testing monthly in a non-prod environment so we catch a bad abort path before it happens for real
[10:45] Marcus O.: someone in yesterday's leadership sync asked whether we should just move off this ERP hosting provider entirely given this outage
[10:47] Anouk V.: I'd push back hard on that, this is a fixable configuration and process issue, not a fundamental platform problem, migrating hosting providers would be a massive project for a problem we can actually fix directly with the three items above
[10:48] Piotr Z.: agreed, let's not treat a fixable batch-scheduling and failover-abort issue as a reason to rip out the whole platform
[10:50] Anouk V.: I'll file all three fix items as tickets today with owners and target dates
[10:52] Marcus O.: sounds good, want me to draft the summary for tomorrow's leadership sync so we can close out that hosting-migration question directly?
[10:53] Anouk V.: yes please, and include the timeline for all three fixes so they can see this isn't an open-ended risk, it's three concrete, scoped items
[10:55] Piotr Z.: I'll review the draft before it goes out, want to make sure the replication-lag explanation is clear for a non-technical audience
